title: The Critical Line
chapters: The critical strip, the exact target, and the role of Dirichlet characters.
Prime powers and the Mellin transform
Follow one prime power from an Euler product to a residue.
Factorials, local coordinates, and the cost of mixed derivatives.
From the global theta function to an integral jet
Follow an integral expansion through torsion translation and a change of local frame.
Lattices and the arithmetic main term
Transporting a bound through metrics, ranks, and normalized maps.
Theta lifts, local factors and the Galois input
Follow the pair used for the Galois construction and compute the local factors that keep an iterated lift nonzero.
Character averaging and the costs that a square-root estimate must absorb.
How class groups, cyclotomic descent and signed character estimates supply one arithmetic window.
How derivatives concentrated on distant intervals exclude a pole.
Removing Euler factors, exchanging characters, and returning to zeta.
glossary: A compatible list of local entries, one in each completion of a number field, integral at all but finitely many finite places. The diagonal embedding sends one field element to its value in every completion.
An extension agreeing with a given analytic function on its original domain. Agreement on an open subset determines the continuation on a connected domain.
The characters of a finite abelian group that are identically one on a specified subgroup. Subgroup averaging selects exactly these characters.
A function on an adelic group that descends under its rational subgroup and satisfies the prescribed regularity and other conditions. Square-integrability on the quotient matters for the lifts here.
A finite linear combination of ordered words in a group. Its boundary takes alternating faces obtained by omitting an end entry or multiplying neighboring entries.
A weighted finite sum of Bernoulli polynomial values at fractions of the conductor. The minus estimate clears its denominators and uses the same algebraic integer at every coefficient prime.

In the coefficient sequence for reduction modulo q, lift a cycle to an integral chain. Its boundary is a multiple of q. Dividing that boundary by q gives a class one degree lower, killed by q. This map distinguishes the two torsion orders in the cycle count.
A homomorphism from a finite group to nonzero complex numbers. A Dirichlet character extends by zero off the units modulo N.
Fractional ideals of the number field K modulo principal fractional ideals. The quotient Cl(K)/ℓCl(K) measures the number of independent characters of order ℓ.
A function c satisfying c(gh)=c(g)+g·c(h). Its class in degree one identifies functions differing by g↦g·a−a. Local conditions impose restrictions on these classes.
A linear functional that vanishes on boundaries. For the residue test, consecutive pairs contribute carries and the last entry contributes an additive index.
The least divisor of the modulus from which a Dirichlet character is induced. A primitive character has conductor equal to its modulus.
The volume of a fundamental parallelepiped of a lattice in its real span with the chosen metric.
The region 0 < Re s < 1. Here s = σ+it; σ = ½ is the critical line.
A stage in a tower formed by adjoining roots of unity. In the ℓ-adic tower here, layer m has relative degree ℓᵐ over the chosen base field.
A ring in which each nonzero element has the form uπⁿ for a unit u, a fixed uniformizer π and a nonnegative integer n. This exponent measures divisibility. For ℤℓ one can take π=ℓ.

An integral obtained by placing two copies of a unitary group in a larger group and pairing a section there with matrix coefficients on the original copies. Its local factors determine the partial L-function in the theta norm.

A pair of full local lattices can be put into diagonal form by integral changes of bases. The integer exponents of a uniformizer classify their relative position. Their sum gives the determinant valuation and the sum of their absolute values gives the degree in the split-place series.
The limit of 1+1/2+⋯+1/n − log n; it is the constant Laurent coefficient of ζ at 1.
A group law in power series at the identity and a change of coordinate taking that law to addition.
Inertia is the subgroup of a local Galois group acting trivially on the residue field. A Frobenius class acts there by raising to the residue-field size.
A translation-invariant measure on a locally compact group. Its normalization matters when comparing the two sides of the Petersson identity.
The scalar formed by translating one vector by a group element and pairing it with a second vector. When the vectors coincide, its value at the identity is their squared norm.
Here the integral from 1 to infinity against x^(−s−1) dx. Under x=eᵘ it becomes a Laplace transform.
Number of simple quotients in a composition series. For a finite ℤℓ-module of order ℓᵈ the length is d. Its minimum number of generators can be smaller.
At an isolated zero ρ, the integer m≥1 such that L(s)=(s−ρ)ᵐh(s) with h holomorphic and h(ρ)≠0. The balance chapter also uses m for a chain length.
The integral of the product of an automorphic function and the complex conjugate of another on the automorphic quotient, with the chosen measure. On the diagonal it gives a squared norm.
The residue is the coefficient of (s−ρ)⁻¹ in a Laurent expansion. A simple pole has a nonzero residue and no higher-order singular terms.
The number max(u,0). In a ramp it cuts off the sum; in the window estimate it keeps the side controlled by the hypothesis.
The multiplicity of a prime in the extended prime ideal. It enters the weighting of the finite-place contributions to divisibility.
The degree of an extension of residue fields. In an unramified quadratic extension, a split base prime has two primes of residue degree one. An inert prime has one of degree two.
The saturation of Λ in E is the set of x in E such that kx lies in Λ for some nonzero integer k. Modulo Λ it gives exactly the torsion subgroup of E/Λ.
A direct sum of irreducible representations. One can compare multiplicities constituent by constituent once an isomorphism of the global representations has been established.
The subgroup of degree-one Galois cohomology classes whose restrictions at the specified places vanish. Its module length enters the cohomological window bound.
Homology with an induced coefficient module can be computed in the subgroup. Here the module of functions on a finite cyclic quotient turns a homology calculation for G into one for the kernel.
For a Euclidean lattice of positive rank, its Arakelov slope is the negative log of its covolume divided by its rank. Extremal slopes measure sublattices and quotients.
At a good finite place the vectors are fixed by the specified maximal compact subgroup. This invariance permits the local integral to be evaluated by Hecke eigenvalues.

The subgroup of symmetries that take an object to itself. In the arithmetic face count a finite stabilizer acts faithfully on a finite set of shortest vectors. Its order contributes to the bound for integral homology.
An element of a group ring acting on ideal classes in cyclotomic arithmetic. Its annihilation property supplies a relation on a quotient of the class group in the tower argument.
A change in a Galois action by a power of the cyclotomic character, which records the action on roots of unity. Its exponent matters in a local restriction kernel.
An integral operator with a theta kernel carrying an automorphic function between spaces for two groups.
The exponent of p in a nonzero rational number, extended by vₚ(0)=+∞. The normalized p-adic absolute value is p to the power −vₚ.
Λ(pʲ)=log p for a prime p and integer j≥1; its value at every other positive integer is zero.
An interval [Y,Y¹⁺ᵟ] with δ>0; in logarithmic coordinates its endpoints are U=log Y and (1+δ)U.
Largest dimension of a subspace on which the entire Hermitian pairing vanishes. It determines which convergence hypothesis is required for the doubled theta integral.
